item.title: Hida Beef: Gifu's Premium Marbled Wagyu — Guide
item.description: Hida beef is one of Japan’s top premium wagyu brands, produced from black-haired cattle raised in the Hida region of Gifu and prized for its fine, delicate marbling, melt-in-the-mouth tenderness and rich, sweet flavour. It is served across Takayama and the wider region in many forms, from steak and hoba-miso (grilled over a magnolia leaf with miso) to Hida beef sushi, croquettes and grilled skewers sold as street food in the old town, giving visitors plenty of ways to sample it at every price point.

item.title: Takayama Sanmachi Suji: A Beautifully Preserved Merchant Old Town — Guide
item.description: Sanmachi Suji is the beautifully preserved heart of Takayama’s old town, a cluster of narrow lanes lined with dark wooden merchant houses dating from the Edo period, when the town prospered as a centre of skilled carpenters and merchants in the mountainous Hida region. Today the lanes are home to sake breweries marked by cedar-ball signs, cafes, craft shops, and stalls selling Hida beef and local sweets, making it one of Japan’s most atmospheric and enjoyable historic districts to explore on foot.

item.title: Gifu Food Guide: Hida Beef, Sake Breweries & Mountain Cuisine
item.description: The food culture of Gifu Prefecture is inseparable from its geography. Surrounded by mountains on three sides, cut off from the coast and its seafood, the Hida and Mino regions developed a cuisine built around what the highlands provided in abundance: river fish, mountain vegetables foraged from steep valley slopes, wild game, fermented foods preserved through long winters, and rice grown in terraced paddies. The result is a table that rewards curiosity — unfamiliar ingredients prepared with generations of accumulated knowledge, and sake breweries that have been making Hida rice wine since the seventeenth century.

item.title: Gifu Top Sightseeing: Shirakawa-go, Takayama & Cormorant Fishing
item.description: Gifu Prefecture occupies the mountainous heart of Honshu, a landlocked expanse of deep valleys, ancient cedar forests, and river gorges that stretches from the Northern Alps down to the Nobi Plain. It is a prefecture of genuine superlatives: one of Japan’s three great onsen towns, a UNESCO World Heritage village that looks unchanged from the eighteenth century, a mountain town preserved so completely that it earned the name Little Kyoto of the Alps, and a cormorant fishing tradition that has continued unbroken for thirteen hundred years.

item.title: Takayama and Shirakawago Travel Guide 2026
item.description: Takayama and Shirakawago Travel Guide: Your Complete Insider’s Guide to Japan’s Mountain Heart Tucked into the northern Japanese Alps of Gifu Prefecture, Takayama is one of those rare places in Japan where time genuinely slows down. The Edo-period streets aren’t reconstructions — they’re the real thing, preserved for over 400 years with their dark-timbered merchant houses, sake breweries, and morning markets that have run continuously since the 1600s. If you’re searching for a comprehensive Takayama and Shirakawago travel guide, you’ve found the right one.
